title: London woman loses 48cm boundary fight over neighbour’s kitchen extension
description: In a surprising turn of events, a homeowner in Surbiton, London, lost a legal dispute concerning a narrow 48-centimetre strip of land. It was determined that the neighbours' kitchen extension had effectively claimed squatters' rights, having occupied the land uncontested for over two decades. The First-tier Tribunal's decision highlights crucial insights into property borders and emphasizes the importance of diligent title plan checks for prospective buyers to avoid future complications.

title: US says Europe refused to join push for tariffs on India, China over Russian oil

Bessent emphasized the need for the US to reassess its strategy regarding sanctions and tariffs, especially with respect to energy supplies.

He stated his decision was for the future of the state and would respect the party's ticket offering. Akoijam currently faces serious allegations of sexual harassment and has been dismissed from Jawaharlal Nehru University. Multiple complaints from female students prompted a police investigation into his conduct and actions.

title: Centre tells Meta to overhaul content promotion system on Facebook, Instagram

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology released an advisory emphasizing due diligence under the IT Rules. It highlighted the need for rapid identification and review of content with public disturbance potential. Additionally, Meta must assist law enforcement agencies by providing necessary information promptly.

title: Shafali Verma scripts history with ninth 50-plus score as India thrash Zimbabwe to seal T20I series
description: Shafali Verma's explosive 25-ball 55 propelled India to a dominant nine-wicket victory over Zimbabwe in the second T20I, securing a 2-0 lead in the series. This remarkable performance marked Verma's ninth fifty-plus score in women's T20Is within this calendar year. Partnered with Smriti Mandhana, who contributed 47 runs, they set a record with nine 50-plus partnerships in 2026.

description: Amazon has warned it could shut 15 warehouses and move thousands of delivery jobs out of New York City over the Delivery Protection Act, a labour bill backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani. The bill would require Amazon to directly employ 5,000 contracted delivery drivers. Logistics experts say the retail giant is likely to follow through, pointing to its decision to close seven warehouses in Montreal, Canada, after a union drive.

title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa emergency: How Pak's policies fueled province's security crisis
description: Pakistan has declared a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, suspending the regional government and centralizing control. This decision comes in response to the deteriorating security situation and ongoing protests against the authorities. The move has prompted a crackdown on opposition leaders, further limiting political dissent and freedom. Additionally, residents are facing renewed uncertainty and instability as military involvement increases in civilian matters.

title: Dipke accuses state of delaying proceedings to prevent release of Saurav Das, Ranka
description: Abhijeet Dipke accused the state of deliberately prolonging the arrests of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. He claimed they are using delaying tactics to obstruct court proceedings and prevent their release. The Cockroach Janta Party plans to take legal action if the individuals are not released soon. CJP's legal head, Ratna Singh, criticized the Special Executive Magistrate for arbitrary behavior during the hearings.

title: Asian Para Games: Can India script another 100-medal triumph despite smaller contingent?
description: India will be represented by 166 athletes across 10 disciplines at the October 18-24 event. The contingent features several Paralympic medallists, world champions and emerging talents, including archer Sheetal Devi, badminton stars Pramod Bhagat and Suhas Yathiraj, and para-table tennis player Bhavina Patel.

title: Pakistan plans Moon landing by 2035, expands space cooperation with China
description: Pakistan aims to land on the Moon by 2035 and send its first astronaut for a space mission. The astronaut, selected from candidates trained in China, is expected to participate in scientific experiments. Cooperation with China enhances Pakistan's aspirations in space exploration and technological advancement. Additionally, plans for establishing the first Space Museum at the University of Narowal were announced to promote scientific awareness.

title: Tiger Shroff shot at: Video captures sounds of gunshots - watch
description: Amidst the excitement of a football match in Mumbai, chaos ensued when gunshots rang out from motorcycle-riding attackers. Fans eagerly awaiting a glimpse of Tiger Shroff were thrown into panic. Thankfully, Tiger remained unharmed, yet both his driver and an autorickshaw driver required medical attention. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang has allegedly claimed responsibility, but verification is pending. The Mumbai Crime Branch continues to investigate the incident thoroughly.

title: 7 rounds fired, 3 attackers: Tiger Shroff escapes assassination bid; manhunt launched
description: On a dramatic Sunday evening in Juhu, Mumbai, shots were fired at actor Tiger Shroff's vehicle. Thankfully, police confirm that Shroff remained unharmed. The incident took place close to Pushpa Park, prompting a thorough investigation. Authorities are reviewing CCTV footage to track down the shooters, and a manhunt is underway to capture those behind this alarming attack.

Despite her denial, the police are intensifying their search for her and others involved. The investigation continues as authorities seek further evidence regarding the circumstances of his death.

title: 8 workers killed as speeding car runs them over in Punjab’s Sangrur

The local populace criticized the emergency responders for their slow arrival, igniting protests in the region. Police have detained individuals from the vehicle, although the driver has yet to be caught.

title: Manipur in turmoil again: 15 houses torched; 1 killed, several injured in gun attack
description: In Chassad village, located in Manipur's Kamjong district, at least 15 houses were burned late Saturday night. Suspected militants attacked the village, causing significant chaos and civilians to flee for safety. A Kuki civilian was killed during the assault, and four others suffered injuries from gunfire. Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen condemned the violence and called for strict action against the perpetrators.

These attacks have targeted key infrastructure, including Riyadh’s international airport and Saudi Aramco. Egypt has previously supported Saudi Arabia in the Yemeni conflict, although its role has been limited.

title: 'BJP conspiring to add fake votes': Akhilesh makes big claim, questions need for SSR

He urged party workers to remain vigilant at polling booths and defend against electoral malpractice. Yadav raised concerns over the Election Commission's rationale for revising electoral rolls, questioning the need for it. He also criticized the BJP government's performance on various issues impacting citizens, including education and corruption.

With more than 500 police officers reported injured and severe property destruction across various cities, officials in both Belgium and Italy have condemned the clashes while understanding the underlying issues.

The crowded conditions worsened by rain contributed significantly to the tragic event. Adhikari criticized the previous TMC administration for leaving behind issues that led to this disaster. Additionally, seven individuals connected to the incident have been remanded to police custody for further questioning.

title: JD Vance’s immigration tiger is turning on its rider
description: US Vice President JD Vance admitted his rhetoric on H-1B visas was flawed during a recent town hall event. An Indian-American woman challenged him on his stance, suggesting it scapegoats immigrants. Vance defended his position by claiming he was criticizing corporate practices rather than foreign workers. His remarks have led to significant backlash from various groups regarding his mixed heritage.

title: Russia sold Alaska for peanuts. Now it guards America against Moscow
description: In 1867, Russia sold Alaska to the United States for $7.2 million, reflecting strategic concerns. The decision stemmed from fears of potential conflict with Britain during the Crimean War. Subsequent discoveries of natural resources transformed Alaska's economic importance significantly over the years. Alaska emerged as a crucial military platform for the United States against the Russian Far East.

title: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days if US accepts conditions
description: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi reiterated that the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remains in place. Tehran is analyzing the US response regarding its conditions for ending the conflict. These conditions include lifting sanctions and ending aggression in the region. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump expressed optimism about a swift resolution to the war and lower gas prices.

This stellar performance not only played a pivotal role in Zimbabwe's 99-run victory but also showcased a promising partnership with Craig Ervine, who contributed 93 runs. Zimbabwe's bowlers were equally impressive, dismissing Bangladesh for 172 runs, marking a historic day in Zimbabwean cricket.

title: ‘Consistency is overrated’: Ex-cricketer explains fine line between form and failure
description: "He is never out of form. The kind of player Sanju Samson has been in the T20 format; his form fluctuates. But it is always a matter of one innings. He plays one good innings, and he is back in form."

title: Google Maps route likely led truck to Gwalior temple: Police
description: Around 1.30 am on Sunday, a heavy truck collided with devotees at Sheetla Mata Temple in Gwalior. The tragic incident resulted in at least 16 fatalities and numerous injuries among attendees. Authorities are investigating how the truck bypassed vehicle restrictions near the temple during the festival. Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed distress, offering condolences and financial support for the victims’ families.

title: 'Unacceptable': Paswan defends 'Leave India' notice to Imran Khan over Mumbai stir

description: In Utah, a dedicated couple has poured $2 million into an extraordinary backyard pool designed specifically for scuba diving. This stunning installation boasts a remarkable 90-foot artificial mountain, five magnificent waterfalls, and an exhilarating underwater tunnel. By creating such a bespoke sanctuary, they provide a fantastic recreational escapade for scuba lovers, complete with a lazy river and a fully equipped kitchen set within the mountain's embrace.

title: France's 140 year old Town Hall survived World Wars but succumbed to protesters

description: Sergey Brin has made a significant contribution against California's proposed billionaire wealth tax to avoid financial impacts. After relocating to Nevada, he is no longer eligible to vote on this measure. This one-time tax is set to apply only to California residents from 2026 if approved. Other tech billionaires like Eric Schmidt and Peter Thiel have joined Brin in opposing the tax.

title: How Tom Brady's childhood love for baseball cards inspired his business
description: Tom Brady's love for baseball cards began in his youth and has only deepened over the years. His treasured collection of Don Mattingly cards symbolizes his lifelong enthusiasm. Now, as a co-owner of CardVault, he is dedicated to enhancing the store's impact in the trading card world. Brady aims to enrich inventory and elevate customer experiences, striving to motivate a fresh wave of collectors through his entrepreneurial ventures.

title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf raise $300,000 for charity with 20 luxury watches
description: In 2018, Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf celebrated their partnership with Longines by organizing a charity auction. The auction raised $300,000 for their respective foundations, supporting education and children's trauma recovery. The event took place at the Musée Rodin in Paris, highlighting their decade-long collaboration with the watchmaker. Graf's foundation, Children for Tomorrow, expanded its reach into schools thanks to newfound funding.
